name: Maisie's Galaxy
note: One of the first z>11 galaxies spectroscopically confirmed by JWST; named after Finkelstein's daughter.

name: GN-z11
note: Luminous z=10.6 galaxy, longtime distance record-holder pre-JWST; N-rich UV spectrum.

name: CEERS-93316
note: Famous z_phot~16.4 candidate later revised to a z=4.91 dusty galaxy - cautionary tale.

name: JADES-GS-z14-0
ref: Carniani+2024; z spec refined by ALMA [OIII]88um (Carniani+2025, Schouws+2025)
note: Current most-distant spectroscopically confirmed galaxy (z=14.18).

name: JADES-GS-z14-1
note: Faintest spectroscopically confirmed galaxy at z~14.

name: JADES-GS-z13-0
note: One of first four z>10 galaxies spectroscopically confirmed by JWST; was distance record-holder 2022-2024.

name: JADES-GS-z12-0
note: One of the original four Curtis-Lake z>10 confirmations.

name: JADES-GS-z11-0
note: One of the original four Curtis-Lake z>10 confirmations.

name: JADES-GS-z10-0
note: One of the original four Curtis-Lake z>10 confirmations; historically the UDFj z-drop.

name: JADES-GS-z13-1
note: z~13 galaxy with strong Lyman-alpha damping-wing / possible Lyman-alpha; probes reionization.

name: MoM-z14
ref: Naidu+2025 ('A Cosmic Miracle', Open J. Astrophys.)
note: Most distant spectroscopically confirmed galaxy as of 2025 (z=14.44); first result from the 'Mirage or Miracle' survey in COSMOS.

name: GHZ2
note: Luminous z=12.3 galaxy behind Abell 2744; one of the brightest known ultra-high-z sources.

name: GHZ1
note: Bright z~9.9 galaxy behind Abell 2744, early GLASS-JWST z>10 candidate.

name: GHZ9
note: z=10.1 source in Abell 2744 with an X-ray-detected accreting SMBH (dual AGN + star formation).

name: UNCOVER-z13
note: Lensed z~13 galaxy behind Abell 2744 (tentative spec confirmation via break).

name: UNCOVER-z12
note: Lensed z=12.4 galaxy behind Abell 2744.

name: Abell2744-QSO1
note: Prototypical 'little red dot' - a triply-lensed, reddened z=7.04 AGN with ~50M-solar SMBH; high BH-to-host mass ratio.

name: CEERS 1019
note: Hosted the most distant confirmed accreting SMBH at the time (z=8.68, 570 Myr after Big Bang); originally EGSY8p7.

name: CEERS-2112
note: Most distant barred spiral galaxy found; a young Milky-Way analog / progenitor at z=3.

name: GNz7q
note: Dust-reddened compact quasar precursor bridging starbursts and quasars at cosmic dawn in GOODS-N.

name: Gz9p3
note: Bright interacting/merging system at z=9.3 lensed by Abell 2744 periphery (mu~1.7).

name: The Cliff
note: Famous 'little red dot' in PRIMER-UDS with the strongest Balmer break yet seen plus broad H-alpha; the most notable nicknamed UDS object.

name: COSMOS-Web ring
note: Serendipitous Einstein ring in COSMOS-Web; massive quiescent elliptical lens (z_lens~2.0) around a z=5.10 spec source.

name: Cosmic Grapes
note: Quintuply-imaged rotating disk resolved into ~15 star-forming clumps ('grapes') at z=6.07.

name: Firefly Sparkle
note: Lensed Milky-Way-progenitor arc resolved into individual star clusters at z=8.3.

name: GLIMPSE-16a
note: Robust z~16.4 photometric candidate behind lensing cluster Abell S1063.

name: GLIMPSE-16b
note: Robust z~15.8 photometric candidate behind Abell S1063.
